Description: Map width in tiles (every tile is 16x16 pixels).
Map height in tiles.
How many tiles start with a tree (scattered everywhere).
How many tiles have a grass tuft (grass-detail.png).
On average a new tree grows somewhere every this many seconds (until there are tree.maxFactor times the trees there were at the start).
The forest stops growing at this many times the number of trees it started with (1.1 = ten percent more).
A new tree fades in over this long.
How much darker the grass tufts are drawn than their picture (the ground itself is not changed). 0 = as painted, higher = darker.
Allowed zoom levels. Only whole numbers, so every pixel stays the same size.
Smallest readable name size on screen.
Name size in world pixels (scales with zoom; never smaller than render.nameFontMinPx on screen).
The sun is always in the same place. How far shadows lean sideways (negative = to the left).
How long shadows are on the ground (up and down).
Tree opacity while a unit stands behind it.
How fast the tree fades.
How high a body hops while walking, in pixels.
Where the middle of the knight's body is inside its 16 pixel picture (it turns around this point).
Where the middle of the body is inside its 16 pixel picture (it turns around this point).
Where the middle of the farmer's body is inside its 16 pixel picture (it turns around this point).
How many letters of a speech bubble appear per second (each one makes a sound).
Syllables used to build names (units and kingdoms).
Words that must never appear in a name, not even inside a longer name (checked after the name is made, so it is simply made again). Add anything you spot.
The consonants a name of the third kind can end in.
Chance weight of a name with 2 syllables (the three chances are compared with each other, so 33 / 33 / 33 means one third each).
Chance weight of a name with 3 syllables.
Chance weight of a name with 2 syllables that ends in one of the consonants below.
How fast the knight walks.
The neighbour's name.
What the neighbour is. Tero is a knight now (he fights slimes).
Which picture in assets/sprites the neighbour uses (the knight).
How fast the neighbour strolls.
A speech bubble stays this long after the last letter.
Overall loudness of the voices.
How long each letter's beep lasts.
How far away a voice can be heard at all. The closer you are, the louder, and far voices also sound duller and come from their side.
How much each sound leans toward the pitch of the next sound (0 = not at all, 1 = fully reaches it). Up if the next sound is higher, down if lower.
How much the voice rises at the end of a question. 1 = the original gentle rise, 1.4 = a little more, 2.5 = very exaggerated.
Base pitch of the neighbour's beeps. Higher is squeakier, lower is calmer.
How much sparkle the neighbour's beep has (0 = a plain soft tone, 1.5 = very sparkly).
Where the middle of the slime is inside its 16 pixel picture (it turns around this point).
How far a normal dodge goes.
How long a dodge takes.
While dodging nothing can hurt the dodger (a little longer than the dodge itself).
Wait after a dodge before the next one.
Hearts of a knight. (Nothing is shown on screen yet.)

Hitboxes are squares. A knight's square is centred on its feet and is this big from the middle to the side (0.22 = 0.44 tiles wide). Units and trees are solid for each other; press H in the game to see the squares.
The same for a slime's square.
The same for a tree: its square is the trunk (the leaves are only decoration you can walk behind).
A slime jump hurts whoever's square it touches, this much bigger than the squares themselves.
A knight gets one heart back this often when not hit.
A defeated knight is gone (it flies away and flickers out) and then stays away this long before it comes back, flickering, where it landed.
After being hit nothing can hurt you for this long.
How far a hit pushes you back.
How long the white flash lasts after a hit.
How far a knight slash reaches.
The slash sweeps this wide.
The knight stops and prepares this long before the slash starts.
How long the slash sweep takes.
Wait after a slash before the next one.
Damage of a slash.
How far a slash pushes a slime back.
A knight neighbour notices slimes this close and fights them.
How early (before the slime jumps) the knight starts a dodge, at the earliest. He never dodges before the slime has chosen its direction.
...and at the latest.
Chance that the knight sees an attack coming and dodges it.
Chance that a knight reads YOUR slash and dodges it. Lower = you hit more often.
How long after you start a slash a knight needs (at least) to react to it. Your slash takes about a third of a second, so slower reactions mean it often lands.
...and at most.
In a fight with you a knight feints (a quick dodge sideways) about this often while he circles you. 0 = never.
How far a feint dodge goes.
How long Tero treats you as an enemy after you attacked him. Every new attack renews it. He forgives you when it runs out, or when one of you is defeated.

The "!" over a head when somebody decides to fight (a knight you hit or swung at, a knight that sees a slime, a slime that notices somebody): he stands still this long (at least) and then fights. It shows only at the start of a fight, never before an attack.
...and at most this long.
Knights and slimes show the "!" only when they start fighting. After this long with nothing to fight they are calm again, and the next fight starts with a new "!".
How many knights there are (Tero and the others, not counting you). A knocked-out knight comes back after unit.knockedOutSeconds, so there are always this many.
The knights start scattered within this many tiles of the middle of the map (where you start too).
A knight that sees no slime close by walks toward the nearest slime if it is closer than this.
How fast a knight walks toward a slime it hunts.
Tero (the one you talk to) does not hunt slimes farther than this from you, and walks back to you when he has strayed farther, so you can always hear him. The other knights roam freely.
How dangerous Tero judges you compared to a slime. Higher = he goes for you before the slimes; 0.5 = he mostly ignores you while slimes are around.
How fast the knight neighbour walks in a fight.
Hearts of a slime (a slash takes 1).
How fast a slime creeps toward the nearest unit.
A slime goes for the nearest unit if it is this close.
A slime starts its attack (a dodge that hurts) from this far.
How long a slime squashes and shakes before it jumps. This is the warning.
The slime picks its direction this long before it jumps, so you can dodge sideways.
How far the slime jumps.
How long the jump takes.
Rest after a jump.
Units this close to a jumping slime get hit.
Damage of a slime jump.
A slime that was slashed cannot act this long.
The first slime appears this long after you start.
A replacement slime appears after at least this long (when fewer than slime.maxAlive are alive)...
...and after at most this long.
How many slimes there are. The world starts with this many, and whenever one is defeated another one appears somewhere on the map.
Slimes appear at least this far from you...
...and at most this far.
Width of the health bar over a head: this many game pixels per heart.
Height of the health bar over a head, in game pixels (plus a 1 px frame).
How far a defeated body is flung away.
How long the flight takes (it tumbles in quarter turns and hops twice).
It lies still this long...
...then flickers this long and is gone.
A defeated body flung through grass sends the tufts flying. 0 = the grass stays. (Trees and units are never smashed: bodies bounce off them.)
How wide the path of a flung body is for grass (grass closer than this to its path is flung away).
How hard smashed trees and grass are launched compared to the defeated body (0.3 = about a third as far; they also turn only 2 or 3 quarter turns and fly lower).
A flung body that hits a tree, a unit or the map edge bounces off and keeps this share of its speed.

0 = tumbling bodies and flung trees/grass turn perfectly smoothly (while turning, their pixels are turned too, so they look slanted; they are square again when they lie still). 1 = every frame is re-painted onto the game pixels so all pixels stay square, but the edges shimmer.
Smashed grass grows back after this long. 0 = never.
How strong the screen shake of a hit is in the very middle of the screen, in game pixels (it is stronger the nearer a hit is to the middle; 0 turns shaking off).
A hit that defeats somebody shakes this many times stronger.
How quickly the shake dies down.
1 = every hit on screen shakes it. 0 = only hits you land shake it (and hits on you, if shake.whenPlayerHurt is 1).
1 = you getting hit shakes the screen. 0 = it does not (shake.others and your own hits are separate).
